events.description: Join the National Museum of the American Latino for a festival that explores how families and communities across the United States mark the transition to adulthood. events.description: ABOUT STORYTIME STUDIO Storytime Studio is a captivating blend of play, educator-led read-alouds, and art exploration designed for kids from birth to age 6 and their caregivers. Every Wednesday morning at 10 and 11 AM, visitors are welcomed into our studio to enjoy a special Storytime adventure. Storytime Studio has limited capacity. Entry is first-come, first-served. THIS WEEK Celebrate Art School Spirit Weeks by dressing head-to-toe in your favorite color! With help from artist Joan Mitchell and her painting Cercando un Ago (1959), we’ll explore how different colors make us feel and create our own paintings that express our emotions. Featured book: The Color Monster: A Story About Emotions by Anna Llenas KNOW BEFORE YOU GO Storytime Studio is a one-hour experience. Entry to Storytime Studio is first-come, first-served. When the 10 AM session reaches capacity, you’ll be given the option to return for entry to the 11 AM session. Storytime Studio has limited capacity. We’ll pause further entry when both sessions reach full capacity to ensure a safe and enjoyable experience. Due to limited capacity during this public drop-in program, school, youth, and other large groups of eight or more (adults and children) are encouraged to reserve a group program by contacting HMSGEducation@si.edu . Everyone is welcome. Nursing caregivers are welcome. If there are services or accommodations that can improve your experience (e.g., ASL interpretation, live captioning, etc.), please contact HMSGEducation@si.edu . We appreciate receiving such requests at least one to two weeks in advance. PROGRAM SCHEDULE Session #1 10 AM: Open play (felt, blocks, sketching) 10:15 AM: Read-aloud 10:30 AM: Art-making 10:45 AM: Gallery tour Session #2 11 AM: Open play (felt, blocks, sketching) 11:15 AM: Read-aloud 11:30 AM: Art-making 11:45 AM: Gallery tour All sessions meet in Hirshhorn Art School on the Museum’s Lower Level. events.name: Opening Celebration: Light Is a Plastic Medium
events.description: Celebrate the opening of Light Is a Plastic Medium: The Photography of Carlotta Corpron with a special evening suitable for visitors of all ages. Step inside our survey of work by the American abstract photographer and educator whose investigations into the poetics of light and form and innovative use of technology between the mid 1930s-1950s supported the establishment of photography as fine art. Learn more about Carlotta Corpron (1901-1988), her life and artistic achievements with talks by leading experts in the field including a return visit by Katy Hessel, art historian and founder of @thegreatwomenartists. Attendance will be limited and available on a first-come, first-served basis as gallery space allows. 6 pm: Curator Tour: Betsy Johnson 7 pm: Insights: Katy Hessel on Carlotta Corpron All galleries will be open. Circle back to some of our talked-about exhibitions: Big Things for Big Rooms Mark Bradford: Pickett’s Charge Laurie Anderson: Four Talks Adam Pendleton: Love, Queen Catch Revolutions: Art from the Hirshhorn Collection, 1860–1960 before it closes on Nov. 1. This exploration of the Museum’s extensive holdings received a final rotation. Discover masterworks by major figures like the American modernist painter Jacob Lawrence and contemporary abstractionist Lesley Vance and new acquisitions, including a striking sculpture by Thomas Houseago . events.description: Director’s Cut, 35th Anniversary screening, in 4K Restoration! Watch the Trailer International superstar Maggie Cheung ( In the Mood for Love ) embodies tragic screen siren Ruan Lingyu in this unconventional biopic by Hong Kong New Wave master Stanley Kwan ( Rouge ). Known as the “Greta Garbo of China,“ Ruan was praised for her moving and emotive onscreen presence. But Ruan’s private life began to mirror the melodramas that brought her fame and was frequent fodder for the vicious Shanghai tabloids. This tumult culminated in her suicide at age 24. Kwan and Cheung paint a kaleidoscopic yet intimate portrait of the ill-fated actress, deftly blending lush period drama, archival footage, and metatextual documentary sequences of Cheung reflecting on Ruan’s legacy. The result is, much like the films of Ruan Lingyu themselves, “tender, vivid and almost overwhelmingly moving” ( Time Out ). Description adapted from Film Movement. Director: Stanley Kwan (Hong Kong). Released: 1991. Length: 154 min. Format: DCP. Language: Cantonese, Mandarin, and English with English subtitles. Presented by Fortune Star Media Limited, the restoration of the film was carried out from the original 35mm picture and optical soundtrack negative. The prints were repaired, cleaned, and scanned in Hong Kong, then digitally restored in 4K resolution in Bologna, Italy, by L’Immagine Ritrovata. Endorsed by the director, Stanley Kwan, the color correction was completed by Interface Video Production Ltd in Hong Kong. Copresented with JxJ – DC Jewish Film and Music which will also present two films on similar themes. Educational Partner: George Washington University Chinese Arts & Humanities Initiative . events.name: Virtual Book Club | Martyr! by Kaveh Akbar
events.description: Register to join. Halloween costumes welcome~ Calling all readers! We’re starting a quarterly virtual book club, hosted by NPR’s Emily Kwong. You may recognize her from the hit podcast Inheriting about AAPI family history. Our club will meet once each season, with fresh recommendations from some of our favorite Asian-owned bookstores (including Loyalty Bookstore and Yu & Me Books). Expect: open-ended questions, organic conversation, and a structured activity. To kick off the club, our first book is Martyr! by Kaveh Akbar. Grab a copy from the museum store on your next visit. About Martyr! A newly sober, orphaned son of Iranian immigrants, guided by the voices of artists, poets, and kings, embarks on a remarkable search for a family secret that leads him to a terminally ill painter living out her final days in the Brooklyn Museum. Electrifying, funny, and wholly original, Kaveh Akbar’s debut novel is a paean to how we spend our lives seeking meaning—in faith, art, ourselves, others. Martyr! is a New York Times bestseller, National Book Award finalist, one of The New York Times Book Review ’s 10 Best Books of 2024, and a TIME Must-Read Book of 2024. “Kaveh Akbar is one of my favorite writers. Ever.“—Tommy Orange, Pulitzer Prize–nominated author of There There “ Martyr! is nothing short of miraculous.“— The New York Times Book Review Synopsis adapted from Penguin Random House. Meet Your Host Emily Kwong Emily Kwong (she/her) is an NPR audio journalist working at the crossroads of history, science, and family memory. She is the host of two shows: Short Wave , NPR’s science podcast, and Inheriting , LAist’s show about Asian American and Pacific Islander families. Her reporting style is driven by empathy and context—rooted in a sense of people’s lives continuing on long after the story ends. Season 2 of Inheriting will debut in January 2027 and is about five families shaped by five immigration policies passed down through the generations. You can find her on Instagram @kwongsong. Emily loves to curl up with a good book and her orange cat Zuko. She’s very excited to host the first ever virtual book club for the National Museum of Asian Art. Book cover courtesy of Penguin Random House.

events.name: DC | Día de los Muertos (Day of the Dead)
events.description: Día de los Muertos (Day of the Dead) is a time for commemorating our ancestors. Rather than a period of mourning, it is an occasion for celebrating with family—both living and dead—and honoring the cycle of life. Enjoy family-friendly activities throughout the day, including dance performances by Grupo los Tecuanes, making paper marigolds to be placed on a Catrina statue, and making papel picado (perforated paper decorations) with David Amorozo. Learn how pan de muerto (bread of the dead) is made with Neil Vargas, Jr. Learn about La Catrina and her joyful view of life and mortality by interacting with live Catrinas roaming the festival. Visitors are invited to leave photos and mementos of their loved ones on the ofrenda (altar) or commemorate them by writing their names on a butterfly to attach to the memorial arch. SCHEDULE OF EVENTS LEVEL 3: imagiNATIONS Activity Center 10:30 AM | Story Time Families are invited to an interactive story time featuring the book Día de los Muertos by Roseanne Greenfield Thong. They will have the opportunity to engage with objects from the museum's Teaching Collection such as photographs, textiles, or natural materials to deepen their understanding of Día de los Muertos . Tickets may be needed to enter the imagiNATIONS Activity Center and Story Room. Please see staff at the Level 3 entrance desk for assistance. *Recommended for children ages 3-9 and their caregivers. 11 AM–1 PM, 2–4 PM | Hands On: La Catrina Creations! Celebrate the vibrant artistry of Día de los Muertos by decorating a plaster skull from a variety of La Catrina and Calavera (sugar skull) designs. Using paint markers, participants will create a unique keepsake to take home. LEVEL 1: Potomac Atrium 11 AM, 1 PM, 2:30 PM, and 4 PM | Dance Performances by Grupo los Tecuanes The name of the Danza de los Tecuanes (Dance of the Jaguar) is rooted in the Mixtec understanding of the duality of life and death and the fight of good against evil. The Danza de los Viejitos (Dance of the Old Men) is a humorous dance featuring dancers colorfully dressed as old men. The Flor de Piña (Pineapple Flower) is a folk dance from Oaxaca that features women dancing with pineapples balanced on their right shoulders throughout the routine. Each performance will offer bilingual narration. 11 AM-4 PM | Ongoing Activities Hands On: Paper Marigolds Marigolds, or cempasúchitl , serve a special purpose during Día de los Muertos celebrations. Their petals are used to create a path between the cemetery and the family home. Make your own tissue-paper marigold to take home or create a garland to adorn a nine-foot-tall La Catrina , the iconic skeleton fashionista that has become a symbol of Día de los Muertos. Demonstrations: Papel Picado with David Amorozo Papel picado is the Indigenous art form of hand-cut and die-cut paper banners that dates back to pre-Hispanic Mexico. The banners were originally made from a type of bark paper called amate . Today, papel picado is made by cutting tissue paper into intricate designs for Día de los Muertos and other celebrations throughout the year. Learn how it's made with demonstrations by artist David Amorozo. Demonstrations: Pan de muerto with Neil Vargas, Jr. Learn how pan de muerto (bread of the dead) is made with Neil Vargas, Jr., This round bread is traditionally eaten during Día de los Muertos , at a loved one’s gravesite or by the ofrenda. The bread is usually a soft, sweet, round bun often spiced with anise seeds, orange zest or orange flower water. Live: La Catrina La Catrina , the iconic skeleton fashionista that has become a symbol of Día de los Muertos shares a joyful view of life and mortality. Interact with live Catrinas throughout the day as they roam the festival. Butterfly Memorial Arch Select a butterfly of your choice, write a loved one’s name or a short message, and attach the butterfly to the memorial arch. Museum Ofrenda This temporary display honors those who have passed on with photographs or personal effects of the deceased accompanied by flowers, candles, religious icons, water, salt, and an array of food and drink.
